newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ power co's to trial residential competition.
newsitem.headline: NZ power co's to trial residential competition.

text.p: Electricity suppliers Southpower and United Electricity on Tuesday said they would start trialling a system in December which would introduce genuine competition for residential customers for the first time in New Zealand.
"Two thousand South Island customers will be able to buy their power from a competing power company this year," the South Island companies said in joint statement.
Each retailer would supply electricity to 1,000 residential customers who were currently supplied by the other company in a two-year trial starting on December 1 this year.
"The trial will use a technique known as deemed profiling, which bases a customer's future usage of electricity on assumed patterns of use," the companies said.

"United Electricity and Southpower will be individually responsible for recruiting customers in the other's area. Both companies will continue to compete agressively for each other's customers in other areas, or to enter trials with other companies."
Both had agreed that the new electricity supplier in each area would take over services such as billing customers, accepting and receipting payments, and the customer faults service.

The new supplier would pay the other company for all line and metering charges incurred by customers in the trial. The original supplier would undertake meter reading and provide a deemed profile for each pricing option.
New Zealand launched a wholesale electricity market on October 1 last year, designed to foster competition in all areas of the sector.
However, United Electricity chief executive Antony Fowler said the benefits of competition were still not being enjoyed by residential customers, where it was most needed.
While both companies recognised that deemed profiling was not the perfect answer to competition, they said it was a stepping stone to its introduction in the residential market.

"Deemed profiling provides a platform for competition and will allow and encourage the development of different kinds of technology which will open up the avenues to choice," Southpower Managing director Chris Laurie said.
